title: Byzantine Empire
summary: The Byzantine Empire, also known as the Eastern Roman Empire, lasted from 330, when Constantine established its new capital, to 1453, when Constantinople fell to the Ottoman Turks. Its people called themselves Romans; the name 'Byzantine' was coined by 16th-century historians. A Christian state with Greek as its official language, it was the longest-lasting medieval power, and its influence continues in the religion, art, architecture and laws of many states.

uncertainty.note: Start and end years follow the Library of Congress and World History Encyclopedia. There is no consensus on a foundation date for the polity; other scholars place it in the 4th, 5th, 7th or 8th century.

as_recorded.value: It survived until 1453, when its capital Constantinople fell to the Ottoman Turks.
The Byzantine Empire existed from 330 to 1453.

where.historical_name: Constantinople (founded as New Rome), capital of the Roman Empire known today as the Byzantine Empire; in 1453 the capital of the Ottoman Empire

importance.justification: A thousand-year state that preserved Roman law and Greek learning, carried Christianity across eastern Europe, and stood between the Mediterranean and the Islamic world until 1453.

related.because: The Ottoman capture of Constantinople on 29 May 1453 ended the empire.
